content: Splunk HTTP Event Collector Stream for Bunyan Version 0.11.0 This project provides a Bunyan stream for HTTP Event Collector in Splunk Enterprise and Splunk Cloud. Requirements - Node.js v4 or later. Splunk HTTP Event Collector Stream for Bunyan is tested with Node.js v10.0 and v14.0. - Splunk Enterprise 6.3.0 or later, or Splunk Cloud. Splunk HTTP Event Collector Stream for Bunyan is tested with Splunk Enterprise 8.0 and 8.2.0. - An HTTP Event Collector token from your Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud server. - Bunyan (npm install --save bunyan). Installation First, update npm to the latest version by running: sudo npm install npm -g. Then run: npm install --save splunk-bunyan-logger. Usage See the examples folder for usage examples: - all batching.js: Shows how to configure a Bunyan Stream with the 3 batching settings: batchInterval, maxBatchCount, & maxBatchSize. - basic.js: Shows how to configure a Bunyan stream and send a log message to Splunk. - custom format.js: Shows how to configure a Bunyan Stream to log messages to Splunk using a custom format. - manual batching.js: Shows how to queue log messages, and send them in batches by manually calling flush(). - retry.js: Shows how to configure retries on errors. Support The Splunk HTTP Event Collector Stream for Bunyan is community-supported. 1. You can find help through our community on Splunk Answers (use the logging-library-javascript tag to identify your questions). 1. File issues on GitHub. SSL Note: SSL certificate validation is diabled by default. To enable it, set logger.requestOptions.strictSSL = true on your SplunkStream instance: Basic example Community Stay connected with other developers building on Splunk software. ----------- ------------------------------------------------------- Email devinfo\@splunk.com Issues https\://github.com/splunk/splunk-bunyan-logger/issues/ Answers http\://answers.splunk.com/ Blog http\://blogs.splunk.com/dev/ Twitter @splunkdev License The Splunk HTTP Event Collector Stream for Bunyan is licensed under the Apache License 2.0. content: SplunkBunyanLogger Splunk Bunyan Logger module, to be used with Bunyan. See examples for usage. --- Static Methods Translates a Bunyan logging level number to the name of the level. Parameters - level (number) — A Bunyan logging level integer. See SplunkBunyanLogger.levels Returns - string Creates a Bunyan Stream object with the provided config. Parameters - config (object) — See SplunkStream. Returns - SplunkBunyanStream — A Bunyan Stream object. Enums Bunyan's logging levels. Properties - TRACE (string, default: "trace") - DEBUG (string, default: "debug") - INFO (string, default: "info") - WARN (string, default: "warn") - ERROR (string, default: "error") - FATAL (string, default: "fatal") Default: info

description: A class that implements a raw writable stream.
content: SplunkStream Implements:& x20; {@link https://nodejs.org/api/stream.html stream class stream writable Stream.Writable} A class that implements a raw writable stream. Properties - config (object) — Configuration settings for this SplunkStream instance. - contextQueue (Array.\ ) — Queue of context objects to be sent to Splunk. - error (function) — A callback function for errors: function(err, context). Defaults to console.log both values; --- Constructor Parameters - config (object) — Configuration settings for a new SplunkLogger. - config.token (string) — HTTP Event Collector token, required. - config.name (string, optional, default: "splunk-javascript-logging/0.11.1") — Name for this logger. - config.host (string, optional, default: "localhost") — Hostname or IP address of Splunk server. - config.maxRetries (string, optional, default: 0) — How many times to retry when HTTP POST to Splunk fails. - config.path (string, optional, default: "/services/collector/event/1.0") — URL path to send data to on the Splunk server. - config.protocol (string, optional, default: "https") — Protocol used to communicate with the Splunk server, http or https. - config.port (number, optional, default: 8088) — HTTP Event Collector port on the Splunk server. - config.url (string, optional) — URL string to pass to url.parse. This will try to set host, path, protocol, port, url. Any of these values will be overwritten if the corresponding property is set on config. - config.level (string, optional, default: "info") — Logging level to use, will show up as the severity field of an event, see SplunkLogger.levels for common levels. - config.batchInterval (number, optional, default: 0) — Automatically flush events after this many milliseconds. When set to a non-positive value, events will be sent one by one. This setting is ignored when non-positive. - config.maxBatchSize (number, optional, default: 0) — Automatically flush events after the size of queued events exceeds this many bytes. This setting is ignored when non-positive. - config.maxBatchCount (number, optional, default: 1) — Automatically flush events after this many events have been queued. Defaults to flush immediately on sending an event. This setting is ignored when non-positive. --- Instance Methods A callback function called after sending a request to Splunk: function(err, response, body). Defaults to an empty function. Returns the configuration for this logger. See SplunkStream. Returns - Object — Configuration for this logger. The write() function for SplunkStream. Bunyan will call this function when a user logs a message. See Bunyan raw streams. Parameters - data (object) — The data object is provided by Bunyan. Instance Fields

content: SplunkBunyanStream Properties - level (string) — The logging level for Bunyan. - type (string) — Always raw. - on (function) — Takes an event string, and a callback function. The most useful event to listen for is error. See Node.js events documentation. - setEventFormatter (function) — Overrides the eventFormatter for the underlying SplunkLogger. Takes a callback function parameter: function(message, severity), where message is an object, and severity is a string. - on (function) — Adds a listener to to the SplunkStream object, typically used for the error event. - flush (function) — Manually sends all queued events to Splunk in a single HTTP request. Takes a callback function parameter: function(err, response, body). - stream (SplunkStream) — See SplunkStream
